title: Scalable Low-Energy Molecular Conformer Generation with Quantum Mechanical Accuracy
experiments_summary:
1. **ChEMBL3D Dataset Construction**: Molecules were sourced from ChEMBL v34. Protomers in neutral and non-ionized states were generated using OpenEye FixpKa and merged with original structures. Stereocenters with missing annotation were enumerated using OpenEye Flipper. Reference topologies including hydrogens were created with Open Babel. Initial 3D conformers were generated using OpenEye Omega Classic, then optimized with the FIRE algorithm using a variant of the AIMNet2 neural network potential trained to reproduce DFT energies within a CPCM implicit solvation model. Post-processing included topology validation, energy-based filtering, and deduplication based on relative changes in the distance matrix, yielding ~252 million conformers for ~2.4 million unique structures.

2. **LoQI Model Training**: The LoQI generative model was built on the Megalodon architecture, combining a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) layer for invariant features with an equivariant graph neural network (EGNN) for coordinate updates. Inputs included atom types, charges, bond types, pairwise distances, and dot products. A stereochemical graph augmentation was applied: auxiliary edges encoding E/Z geometry were added around double bonds, and directed/undirected edges encoding R/S configuration were added around stereocenters. Training used a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) with weighted cosine noise schedules, with 25 diffusion steps found sufficient for peak performance. The model was trained exclusively to predict atomic coordinates of lowest-energy conformers from ChEMBL3D.

3. **Hold-out Evaluation on ChEMBL3D Test Set**: A hold-out set of 37,075 molecules (not used during training, covering diverse isomeric and protonation states) was used to benchmark LoQI against classical methods (RDKit ETKDG, OpenEye Omega Classic) and retrained generative baselines (DMT-B, Torsional Diffusion). Metrics included median relative energy, fraction of molecules within 0.1 kcal/mol of the dataset minimum, fraction of cases where generated conformers exceeded the dataset reference energy, topology preservation rate, and median relaxation energy after post-generation optimization.

4. **DFT Validation of Below-Reference Conformers**: 88 test-set cases where LoQI generated conformers at least 1 kcal/mol lower in energy than the dataset reference were selected. DFT geometry optimization with a CPCM implicit solvent model was performed on these structures to confirm that energy improvements were not artifacts of the MLIP model.

5. **Stereochemistry Accuracy Evaluation**: LoQI and baselines (RDKit, OpenEye Omega, Torsional Diffusion, DMT-B) were compared on R/S and E/Z stereochemistry preservation accuracy, measured as the fraction of molecules with correctly reproduced stereochemistry at chiral centers and double bonds, respectively.

6. **Scalability Benchmark (ChEMBL3D-XL)**: A subset of ~300 molecules per number of rotatable bonds (spanning up to 25) was constructed. Up to 100 conformers per molecule were generated using LoQI, RDKit ETKDG, and OE Omega Classic, followed by AIMNet2 optimization. Success was defined as generating at least one conformer within 0.1 kcal/mol of the dataset reference minimum. Performance was assessed as a function of the number of rotatable bonds and number of generation trials.

7. **Platinum Diverse Dataset Evaluation**: For each of the 2,879 ligands in the Platinum Diverse dataset, 500 conformers were generated using LoQI and RDKit ETKDG, followed by AIMNet2 optimization. The lowest-energy conformer from each ensemble was identified, and energy differences between the crystal-bound conformer and the predicted minimum were computed. Mean absolute prediction error was assessed as a function of the number of sampled conformers (1 to 99) to evaluate the conformer-count vs. accuracy tradeoff.
